flows.title: Run the quick start check and badge
flows.goal: The user gates the example report against the default minimum and then prints its coverage badge.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate check examples/coverage-summary.json` gates the report against the default minimum of 80% and prints `PASS lines 87.50% (minimum 80.00%)`.
milestones.note: The quick start first verifies that the example report passes the default gate.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate badge examples/coverage-summary.json` reads the report and prints `![lines coverage](https://img.shields.io/badge/lines-87.50%25-green)`.
milestones.note: After the report is checked, the user prints the badge for the same report.

flows.title: Check a selected report successfully
flows.goal: The user checks a report from the working directory with equivalent flag syntax and receives a passing result.

milestones.claimTitle: The optional positional argument to `covergate check` is the path to the report, resolved against the working directory.
milestones.note: The user chooses which coverage summary to check.

milestones.claimTitle: A flag value supplied separated from the flag and a flag value supplied joined with `=` mean the same thing.
milestones.note: The user can provide option values in either documented form before running the check.

milestones.claimTitle: When the selected `total.<metric>.pct` is at or above the minimum, including exactly equal to it, `covergate check` writes `PASS <metric> <pct>% (minimum <min>%)` to stdout with both numbers to two decimals and exits `0`.
milestones.note: The selected coverage meets the threshold.

flows.title: Report a badge even when coverage fails the gate
flows.goal: The user sees that a failed coverage gate does not prevent badge reporting.

milestones.claimTitle: When the selected `total.<metric>.pct` is below the minimum, `covergate check` writes `FAIL <metric> <pct>% (minimum <min>%)` to stdout with both numbers to two decimals and exits `1`.
milestones.note: The report is below the requested minimum.

milestones.claimTitle: `badge` has no minimum of its own and exits `0` with a badge printed even for a report that `check --min 90` rejects with exit `1`.
milestones.note: The same low-coverage report can still be used to print a badge.

flows.title: Print a coverage badge
flows.goal: The user selects a report and metric and gets a Markdown image badge with the documented colour.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate badge` takes the positional report path and `--metric` values exactly as `check` does.
milestones.note: The user selects the report and metric for badge generation.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate badge` reads the selected coverage percentage and prints a Markdown image to stdout whose alt text is `<metric> coverage` and whose URL is `https://img.shields.io/badge/<metric>-<pct>%25-<colour>` with the percentage to two decimals.
milestones.note: The command turns the selected percentage into the badge Markdown.

milestones.claimTitle: The badge colour is `brightgreen` for percentages 90 and above, `green` for 80 up to 90, `yellow` for 60 up to 80, and `red` below 60.
milestones.note: The generated badge uses the documented colour band for the percentage.

flows.title: Write the badge to a file
flows.goal: The user writes the generated Markdown badge to an output file instead of stdout.

milestones.claimTitle: With `--out <path>`, covergate writes the Markdown plus a newline to that file, creates any missing parent directories, and prints `covergate: wrote <path>` to stdout instead of the badge.
milestones.note: This is the file-output variant of badge generation.

flows.title: Initialize configuration and refuse to overwrite it
flows.goal: The user creates the documented configuration file once and is protected from overwriting it on a later init.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate init` prints `covergate: created .covergaterc.json` and writes the documented `.covergaterc.json` file, comments included, into the working directory.
milestones.note: The user creates the initial configuration file.

milestones.claimTitle: When `.covergaterc.json` already exists, `init` leaves its bytes exactly as they were and exits `2` with `covergate: .covergaterc.json already exists`.
milestones.note: A later init preserves the existing configuration exactly.

flows.title: View usage, command help, and version
flows.goal: The user can discover the top-level commands, inspect command-specific flags, and print the installed version.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate --help` and `covergate` with no arguments print the usage block that lists the three commands and exit `0`.
milestones.note: The user starts by viewing the top-level usage.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate <command> --help` prints that command's usage, lists only that command's defined flags, and exits `0`.
milestones.note: The user then asks for help on one command.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate --version` prints `covergate <version>` and exits `0`.
milestones.note: The user can also verify the installed version.

flows.title: Reject init arguments
flows.goal: The user receives the documented error when passing arguments to init.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate init` with any argument exits `2` with `covergate: init takes no arguments`.
milestones.note: This is an init-specific argument error.

flows.title: Format errors consistently
flows.goal: The user receives errors on stderr with the documented covergate prefix.

milestones.claimTitle: Every error message covergate prints goes to stderr and begins with `covergate: `.
milestones.note: This cross-cutting behavior applies to the CLI error cases.

flows.title: Reject a flag with no value
flows.goal: The user receives the documented error when a value-taking flag is left last without a value.

milestones.claimTitle: A flag written last with nothing after it exits `2` with `covergate: --<name> needs a value`.
milestones.note: This is a flag syntax error path.

flows.title: Reject a flag the command does not define
flows.goal: The user receives the documented error when using an unsupported flag for a command.

milestones.claimTitle: A flag the command does not define exits `2` with `covergate: <command> does not accept --<name>`.
milestones.note: This is a command-specific flag validation path.

flows.title: Reject an unknown metric
flows.goal: The user receives the documented error when selecting an unsupported metric.

milestones.claimTitle: A `--metric` value that is not one of `lines`, `statements`, `functions`, or `branches` exits `2` with `covergate: unknown metric "<name>" (expected one of: lines, statements, functions, branches)`.
milestones.note: This validates the metric value before coverage is read.

flows.title: Reject an invalid minimum
flows.goal: The user receives the documented error when the minimum is not a number from 0 to 100.

milestones.claimTitle: A `--min` value that is not a number between 0 and 100 exits `2` with `covergate: the minimum must be a number between 0 and 100`.
milestones.note: This validates the minimum value before a gate result is reported.

flows.title: Reject an unknown command
flows.goal: The user receives the documented error when the first command word is not defined.

milestones.claimTitle: A first word covergate does not define exits `2` with `covergate: unknown command "<name>"`.
milestones.note: This is the top-level command validation path.

flows.title: Reject unreadable reports
flows.goal: The user receives a documented covergate error when the selected report cannot provide the requested coverage percentage.

milestones.claimTitle: If the report file is missing, not valid JSON, or lacks `total.<metric>.pct`, the command exits `2` and prints the corresponding documented `covergate:` error message.
milestones.note: This covers report input failures before a check or badge can be produced.

flows.title: Reject extra check summary paths
flows.goal: The user receives the documented error when check is given more than one summary path.

milestones.claimTitle: A second positional argument to `covergate check` exits `2` with `covergate: check takes at most one summary path`.
milestones.note: This is the positional-argument validation path for check.

flows.title: Use `.covergaterc.json` settings when gating coverage
flows.goal: The user can run covergate with a local `.covergaterc.json` whose comments, omitted fields, and command-line overrides are handled consistently when gating coverage.

milestones.claimTitle: covergate strips `//` line comments and `/* */` block comments from `.covergaterc.json` before parsing it.
milestones.note: A commented configuration file must be accepted before its settings can be used.

milestones.claimTitle: covergate reads `.covergaterc.json` from the directory the command runs in and uses its settings when gating coverage.
milestones.note: After parsing, the local configuration supplies settings for coverage gating.

milestones.claimTitle: When `.covergaterc.json` leaves out a field, covergate falls back to the built-in defaults: `min` 80, `metric` `lines`, and `summary` `coverage/coverage-summary.json`.
milestones.note: Missing configuration fields are completed with defaults before gating.

milestones.claimTitle: For each setting, covergate uses the command-line value before the `.covergaterc.json` value before the built-in default.
milestones.note: The final setting value follows the documented precedence.

flows.title: Reject `.covergaterc.json` that is not valid JSON
flows.goal: The user gets a clear failure when `.covergaterc.json` cannot be parsed as JSON after comments are stripped.

milestones.claimTitle: If `.covergaterc.json` does not parse as JSON after comments are stripped, covergate exits with code 2 and prints `covergate: .covergaterc.json is not valid JSON`.
milestones.note: This is an error path for an invalid configuration file.

flows.title: Reject `.covergaterc.json` that is not an object
flows.goal: The user gets a clear failure when `.covergaterc.json` parses but does not contain a JSON object.

milestones.claimTitle: If `.covergaterc.json` parses but is not an object, covergate exits with code 2 and prints `covergate: .covergaterc.json must contain a JSON object`.
milestones.note: This is an error path for a configuration file with the wrong top-level type.

flows.title: Initialize configuration and gate coverage with it
flows.goal: The user creates a local covergate configuration file and then runs coverage gating that reads and applies that configuration with documented defaults and overrides.

milestones.claimTitle: `covergate init` prints `covergate: created .covergaterc.json` and writes the documented `.covergaterc.json` file, comments included, into the working directory.
milestones.note: Creates the configuration file used by the later gating command.

milestones.claimTitle: covergate strips `//` line comments and `/* */` block comments from `.covergaterc.json` before parsing it.
milestones.note: The initialized file may include comments, so parsing must handle them before use.

milestones.claimTitle: covergate reads `.covergaterc.json` from the directory the command runs in and uses its settings when gating coverage.
milestones.note: The gating command depends on the file created in the working directory.

milestones.claimTitle: When `.covergaterc.json` leaves out a field, covergate falls back to the built-in defaults: `min` 80, `metric` `lines`, and `summary` `coverage/coverage-summary.json`.
milestones.note: The generated or edited configuration can omit settings while still producing a complete gate.

milestones.claimTitle: For each setting, covergate uses the command-line value before the `.covergaterc.json` value before the built-in default.
milestones.note: The final gate uses command-line overrides, then configuration, then defaults.
